I was tired of fighting my UI library

I have rebuilt my blog four times in six years. Each time I picked a popular component library, and each time I ended up in the same place, rebuilding many components from scratch.

So when people started talking about shadcn/ui, I was skeptical. Another library? But it is not a library. You run a command, and the source code for a button lands in your project. Not a package. Not a wrapper. The actual file.

That sounds like a small detail. It is not. It changes who is in charge of your UI, and it took me a few weeks to realize how much I had been designing around other people's decisions.

What owning the code actually means

With a traditional library, customization is a negotiation. You read the docs, find the right prop, and hope the maintainers anticipated your use case. With shadcn/ui, you open the file and change it.

  • No version lock-in. Upgrades are opt-in, one component at a time.
  • No theme API to learn. Styling is plain{" "} Tailwind CSS and CSS variables.
  • Accessibility built in. Under the hood:
    • Radix UI or Base UI handle focus and keyboard behavior
    • ARIA attributes are already wired up

I used to think the hard part of a UI library was the components.{" "} I was wrong. The hard part was finding the right prop accepting that I could just edit the file.

The best component library is the one you can delete a line from without asking anyone for permission.

Rebuilding the post page from scratch

The page I cared about most was the article itself. The one you are reading right now. I wanted a calm reading column, a sticky table of contents, and typography that did not need babysitting.

Getting set up

  1. Initialize the project with npx shadcn@latest init.
  2. Add the handful of components the page actually needs.
  3. Pull in a starting layout from Shadcnblocks instead of a blank file. 
        {`npx shadcn@latest add avatar badge separator

# Added
components/ui/avatar.tsx
components/ui/badge.tsx
components/ui/separator.tsx`}

Three components, three files, all of them readable in under a minute. I opened badge.tsx, tweaked the radius, and moved on. No config file, no theme provider, no PR{" "} to someone else's repo.

Small quality-of-life win: the docs have a command menu. Press{" "} ⌘ + K, type a component name, and you are there.

What changed Old blog shadcn/ui rebuild
UI dependencies 1 large package Copied source files
Style overrides Dozens None
Dark mode A plugin and a prayer CSS variables
Time to first post Two weekends One afternoon

What I would tell you before you start

Do not install every component on day one. Add them as you need them. The whole point is a codebase you understand, and that is easier when it grows with the project.1

Do not treat the defaults as sacred either. They are a starting point, not a spec. Change things. That is the deal you signed up for.

And if you want to skip the blank page entirely, start from a finished layout and edit it down. That is what I did with this one. If you build something with it, I would love to see it. Find me on X{" "} or drop a link in the comments.

1 I installed every component on day one. Learn from my mistakes.
